Let \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(x)\), so \(\theta\in(-\pi/2,\pi/2)\) and \(\cot\theta=1/x\).

Using the standard principal range \(\cot^{-1}\in(0,\pi)\):

- If \(x>0\), then \(\cot^{-1}(1/x)=\theta\), so the angle is \(2\theta\).
- If \(x<0\), then \(\cot^{-1}(1/x)=\theta+\pi\), so the angle is \(2\theta+\pi\).

For \(x>0\):
\[
\sin(2\theta)=\frac{2x}{1+x^2}=\frac13
\]
\[
x^2-6x+1=0 \implies x=3\pm2\sqrt2
\]

For \(x<0\):
\[
\sin(2\theta+\pi)=-\sin(2\theta)=\frac{-2x}{1+x^2}=\frac13
\]
\[
x^2+6x+1=0 \implies x=-3\pm2\sqrt2
\]

Thus all solutions are
\[
-3-2\sqrt2,\ -3+2\sqrt2,\ 3-2\sqrt2,\ 3+2\sqrt2.
\]

The answer is \(-3-2\sqrt2, -3+2\sqrt2, 3-2\sqrt2, 3+2\sqrt2\).
